Indicator: What Telangana does well (relative to national avg)
Value: Telangana ranks 5th nationally on per capita GSDP (Rs 420347 in 2024-25; 1.8x national avg) and 8th on total GSDP with 6.8% real growth exceeding national 6.5%. Composite SDG score 74 ranks 9th nationally (national avg 71) with standout scores: Goal 7 Clean Energy (100/100; Achiever; 1st jointly) and Goal 1 No Poverty (91/100; 2nd nationally). LFPR at 68.7% exceeds national avg 64.3%. Own tax revenue at 6.8% of GSDP is among the highest of general category states. Revenue balance turned surplus in 2026-27 BE. Institutional infrastructure - Samagra Vedika | CGG | TRAC | Kakatiya Governance Fellowship | MCRHRDI | Prajavani | Telangana Rising 2047 | SEEEPC caste survey (96.9% HH coverage) - places it among the strongest governance systems nationally. MMR of 45 is among 8 states to have attained SDG target of MMR <=70.

Indicator: Areas where Telangana lags (relative to national avg)
Value: Telangana is among 6 states recording statistically significant increase (>=3pp) in child stunting between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 (28% to 33%). Child anaemia worsened sharply to 70% (+9pp) - all 31 districts in public health concern zone. Female literacy at 57.92% (Census 2011) is among the lowest of large states. ASER 2024: only 18% of Std III-V students can read Std II text. Enrolled students in govt schools fell from 33 lakh (2021-22) to 27.8 lakh (2023-24) - sharp migration to private. Fiscal deficit at 3.0% GSDP is at FRBM ceiling; outstanding liabilities 28.7% GSDP; outstanding guarantees to PSEs equal 14% GSDP (Rs 241743 crore). Sex ratio at birth 894 is one of 3 states below 900. Health infrastructure has significant shortfalls: CHCs are at 69% shortfall vs norm; hospital beds at 0.80 per 1000 vs required 1.0.
